chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The children are playing with walnuts and eggs and are gambling (with these)'. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not eat from it, for it is prohibited.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating food used in children's gambling games according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that nuts or eggs used in children's gambling games are prohibited for consumption, establishing a legal principle where the object of a gambling game becomes forbidden (haram) due to its association with the act of qimar. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transferability of ritual impurity or prohibition from the act of gambling to the items staked, even in casual or childish contexts, ensuring that the proceeds or items do not enter the household as sustenance. It underscores the comprehensive nature of 'qimar' in fiqh, extending beyond formal betting to any game of chance involving stakes.
